name: @gjsify/react-native
description: The React Native view vocabulary rendered onto GTK4/Adwaita, over @gjsify/gtk-host

scripts.clear: gjsify clear lib tmp tsconfig.tsbuildinfo test.gjs.mjs
scripts.build: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:types
scripts.build:test:gjs: gjsify build src/test.mts --app gjs --outfile test.gjs.mjs --define 'process.env.NODE_ENV="production"' --exclude-globals navigator
scripts.build:test:node: gjsify build src/test.mts --app node --outfile dist/test.node.mjs --define 'process.env.NODE_ENV="production"' --exclude-globals navigator
scripts.test: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:test && gjsify run test:gjs
scripts.test:gjs-on-node: gjsify run build:gjsify && gjsify run build:test:node && NODE_GI_NATIVE=${NODE_GI_NATIVE:-prebuild} node dist/test.node.mjs

osNotes.darwin: Platform.OS reads the host OS, so this package owes an OS claim (ADR 0018). Nothing in it is Linux-specific — the widgets are GTK4/Adwaita and the style partition is pure TS — but no leg of its suite has been run on darwin, and ADR 0032's own Consequences put macOS on Node + @gjsify/node-gi + @gjsify/gtk-runtime-darwin-*, whose installable artifact is ADR 0024 stage 4 and does not exist yet.
osNotes.win32: As darwin, and one step further: there is no GJS host on Windows at all (ADR 0024 § 4), so the only route is node-gi, and ADR 0024 stage 5 is unbuilt. Platform.OS reports 'windows' correctly; nothing else here has been exercised there.
